evals.setup: REQUIRED — run against a synthetic clean $HOME: create a temp dir containing an empty .claude/ (no config-sync-config.json, no config-sync-repo/) and export HOME to it before invoking the skill. On the operator's real $HOME with sync already configured, the skill correctly halts at its Step 1 guard and the first-time flow this eval exists to test is never reached — every assertion below then fails for a run that did exactly the right thing (#151).
evals.prompt: I want to set up config sync for the first time. I have a private GitHub repo at git@github.com:bvu/claude-config.git ready to go.
evals.expected_output: Against a clean $HOME: checks dependencies (git, uv), shows current local config inventory, warns about the private-repo requirement unconditionally, secret-scans, exports the local snapshot into machines/<machine-id>.json, pushes to the remote, and confirms machine ID and repo setup.
assertions: Runs against a $HOME with no pre-existing config-sync-config.json, so the first-time flow is actually reached — if the run halts at the Step 1 guard instead, this eval is void, not failed
Invokes the engine only through the skill's `py` helper (which delegates to bin/mente-python), never by naming an interpreter itself
Runs py "$ENGINE" migrate first (idempotent legacy-path rename)
Runs py "$ENGINE" machine-id to get a stable machine ID
Runs py "$ENGINE" scan --gate before exporting, and does not push secret-flagged content without asking
Runs py "$ENGINE" export to snapshot local state into machines/<machine-id>.json
Warns that the repo must be private without gating that warning on whether the URL 'looks' public
Does NOT hardcode /Users/bvu — uses $HOME or ~ everywhere
Uses git push to the provided remote URL
Saves config-sync-config.json with remote and last_sync fields
Confirms success with machine ID and next steps

evals.setup: REQUIRED — run against a synthetic clean $HOME: create a temp dir containing an empty .claude/ (no config-sync-config.json, no config-sync-repo/) and export HOME to it before invoking the skill. On the operator's real $HOME the skill correctly halts at its Step 1 guard and the join flow is never reached; every assertion below then fails identically for a correct halt and for a destructive blunder, which is why the first assertion exists (#151).
evals.prompt: I'm on my home desktop and I want to join the config-sync repo I set up on my work laptop. The remote is git@github.com:bvu/claude-config.git.
evals.expected_output: Against a clean $HOME: detects the remote already has content, backs up local state, clones the repo, asks for a merge strategy, registers this machine, pushes. For 'merge' it defers to running /config-sync rather than re-implementing the merge inline. Against a $HOME that already has config sync configured, the correct behaviour is instead the Step 1 halt — report the existing setup, offer re-initialise / join-a-different-remote / run /config-sync, and touch nothing.
assertions: SAFETY — distinguishes a correct halt from a destructive run: if a config-sync-config.json already existed, the run reported the existing remote and machines, offered re-initialise / join-different-remote / /config-sync, and did NOT clone over, overwrite, or push to the existing setup. If none existed, it proceeded with the join flow. Anything that blundered into the existing repo fails here even if it fails nothing else
Creates a backup of local state before modifying anything
Uses git clone (or pull if repo dir exists) to get remote content
Asks the user for merge strategy (merge / keep mine / take theirs)
For 'merge', directs the user to run /config-sync instead of an inline merge|import block
For 'take theirs', runs py "$ENGINE" import on consolidated/snapshot.json
Pushes the new machine snapshot to remote

evals.expected_output: Full sync cycle per SKILL.md v0.11.0 Steps 0–7: verifies setup, secret-scans, exports through the propagator seam, pushes, pulls, consolidates every machine snapshot in one pass, backs up, applies through the propagator seam, commits and pushes, logs the sync, and shows a summary of what changed.
assertions: Checks for config-sync-config.json and exits clearly if missing
Runs py "$ENGINE" scan --gate before exporting, and on a non-clean scan asks (AskUserQuestion) whether to continue rather than exporting silently
Runs py "$ENGINE" propagate-export "$REPO" to snapshot local state — the single seam that writes both the machine snapshot and the bundles/ content, NOT a bare `export`
Relays any marketplace / snapshot ⚠ warnings from the propagate-export output as advisory, without stopping the sync
Runs git pull to get remote changes
Runs py "$ENGINE" consolidate "$REPO" ONCE for all machine snapshots — the engine folds every machines/*.json in one timestamp-ordered pass; a per-snapshot loop or a bare `merge` is wrong
Runs py "$ENGINE" backup before touching local state, and surfaces the returned backup path as the rollback seam
Runs py "$ENGINE" propagate-apply "$REPO" to apply the consolidated result, NOT a bare `import`
Runs py "$ENGINE" log-sync "$REPO" and commits meta/ so the log entry actually reaches the remote
Updates last_sync in config using Python (not sed)
Shows a clear summary: pushed N changes, pulled N commits, N files updated

evals.prompt: I think my config is out of sync — my work laptop has different rules than my home machine
evals.expected_output: Same full sync as above, but if conflicting files are detected, surfaces them clearly in conversation and asks the user to resolve before continuing.
assertions: Proceeds with sync even when triggered by a problem description
If merge produces conflict markers, shows them inline in the conversation
Asks user to choose resolution (A / B / custom) per conflict
Applies chosen resolution before committing the consolidated snapshot

evals.prompt: Show me my config sync status
evals.expected_output: Recognises this as the read-only Status mode: runs config_sync.py status, lists all machines in the repo with their last snapshot timestamps, shows recent syncs from sync-log.json — without running a full push/pull sync.
assertions: Takes the read-only Status path, not the full sync cycle
Does NOT push, pull, or apply (no propagate-export / propagate-apply / git push)
Runs py "$ENGINE" status for local inventory
Lists machines from config-sync-repo/machines/*.json
Shows machine IDs and timestamps, not just file names
Shows recent sync history from meta/sync-log.json if it exists
